projectedObliquity.source: Esposito et al. (2017), A&A 601, A53 (arXiv:1702.03136), abstract: lambda = 3.5 +/- 6.8 deg for WASP-43b, from the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect in HARPS-N radial velocities; the system is aligned.

source: The star's spin axis lies along WASP-43b's orbit normal on the sky: the sky-projected angle between them is 3.5 +/- 6.8 degrees (Esposito et al. 2017). The pole is computed from the hosted orbit in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-43b.json. No rotation period is measured (Challener et al. 2024 cite only some evidence of rotational modulation longer than 15 days, from Hellier et al. 2011), so the star does not spin.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is WASP-43b's orbit normal (the star's spin axis, prograde with the orbit); +X faces the Sun at the scene epoch, so grid longitude 0 faces Earth; east longitude. No spin is propagated.
qualification: Measured on the sky, assumed along the line of sight: the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect fixes the axis's projection onto the sky, not its tilt toward or away from us, which is taken to equal the orbit's. The orbit's own orientation on the sky is a display convention (ascending node at position angle 0), so the axis shares it. The tilt taken from the orbit agrees with Esposito et al. (2017), who combine the measured 15.6 +/- 0.4 day rotation period (Hellier et al. 2011) with v sin i to get a stellar inclination above 72 degrees (68% confidence). Spin sense and prime meridian are not measured, so no spin is drawn.
